Or maybe the block moves one step per click toward the clicked point? First click: block at (59,4), clicked (53,10) → block moved to (53,10) (6 steps). Hmm, that's not one step.

Then from (53,10) clicking (21,42): no movement. Distance 32. So there's a movement limit? Or (21,42) is invalid for some other reason.
Hmm, wait. Maybe the block can only move to cells on the line that are "empty" (no dot)? The dots are at (21,42),(23,40),…,(57,6). The block moved to (53,10) — that's a dot cell. So no.
Maybe the block moves toward the clicked point by a fixed number of steps? Click (53,10): block at (59,4) → moved 6 steps to (53,10) (exactly to the click point). Click (21,42): block at (53,10) → should move 32 steps but only moved 0? If the max is, say, 10 steps, it should have moved to (43,20). It didn't move at all.
Or maybe the block can only move to the clicked point if the clicked point is within some distance... or maybe the click needs to be "on the block's line of sight"... hmm.
Wait, maybe I misread. Let me re-verify: the current block is still at (52-54, 9-11). Right.

Let me look at the image again: the ball is in the upper right with a gray core, the line goes to the lower left, the purple block is on the line, the purple block in the HUD is at the top center, the white bar is at the bottom.
What if the white bar at the bottom is the "goal line" and the game is: the ball rolls down the line, and I need to place the purple block as a "bumper" to bounce the ball... but the ball doesn't move.
Honestly, the ball might move in an animation that only happens on specific triggers. Let me try clicking the block itself (53,10) — maybe clicking the block makes it "jump" or "activate." Or maybe I should try clicking cells off the line near the block.
Or, the intended mechanic might be: click the block, then click the destination (two-step drag). The first click (53,10) was... hmm, no, the block moved in one click.
Wait, actually — let me re-verify. Maybe the block didn't "move" — maybe there are two purple blocks and one disappeared? No: initially there were two purple nodes (HUD + board). After the click, still two (HUD + board at the new position). So it moved.
Let me test the distance hypothesis: from (53,10), click (49,14) (4 steps away on the line). If the block moves there, the limit is ≥4. Then click (43,20) (10 steps). And so on. Let me also test the reverse direction: click (57,6) (4 steps in the other direction).
Actually, wait. Maybe the block can only move in one direction (away from the ball / toward the bottom)? (59,4)→(53,10) is toward the ball (upper right). Hmm, that contradicts.
Or maybe the block can only move to the clicked point if the path is clear... the path from (59,4) to (53,10) is clear. From (53,10) to (21,42) is also clear (all dots). Hmm.
Let me test: click (49,14).
